item.title: SleeperGem RubyGems Backdoor and HelloNet ViPNet Update Abuse Target Developers and Russian Agencies
item.content:encoded:
SleeperGem: Compromised git_credential_manager, Dendreo, and fastlane RubyGems Drop a Persistent Backdoor — Should Read

A coordinated RubyGems supply-chain attack named SleeperGem published malicious versions of git_credential_manager, Dendreo, and a fastlane plugin that evade CI, target developer machines, download a backdoor, and install persistence. Anyone who installed or required these versions should treat the machine and reachable secrets as compromised, remove the artifacts, and rotate credentials.

  • Between July 18 and July 19, 2026, malicious versions of git_credential_manager, Dendreo, and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab were published to RubyGems.org in a coordinated supply chain attack named SleeperGem.
  • The malicious gems check for continuous integration environment variables such as GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, and CIRCLECI, and exit without action when they detect a build system.
  • On a developer machine, the loader downloads deploy.sh and a native git-credential-manager binary from the attacker-controlled Forgejo host git.disroot.org, with certificate verification disabled and a User-Agent of Git.
  • Version 2.8.3 of git_credential_manager copies the downloaded binary into $HOME/.local/share/gcm/, launches it as a daemon, and installs both systemd user service and cron persistence under the name git-credential-manager.
  • The article advises anyone who installed or required the affected gems on a developer machine to treat the machine and reachable secrets as compromised, remove the dropped daemon and persistence, check for /usr/local/sbin/ping6, and rotate credentials.

Hackers abuse ViPNet software to target Russian govt agencies — Should Read

A threat actor dubbed HelloNet is abusing the local update mechanism of Russia’s ViPNet security software to sideload malware against Russian government and critical-sector organizations. Kaspersky says there is no evidence ViPNet’s update infrastructure was compromised, and attribution to a Chinese-speaking APT is low confidence.

  • An advanced threat actor dubbed HelloNet is abusing the update mechanism for the ViPNet private networking product suite to target Russian organizations, including government agencies.
  • Kaspersky says HelloNet has impacted organizations in Russia’s government, energy, transport, education, and logistics sectors.
  • Attackers placed a malicious wtsapi32.dll file named HelloInjector inside the local ViPNet Update System directory so it would be sideloaded at system startup by the legitimate itcsrvup64.exe process.
  • HelloInjector injects into svchost.exe and runs an embedded payload called HelloProxy in memory, which contacts a command-and-control server to receive additional modules.
  • Kaspersky has tentatively attributed the campaign to an unidentified Chinese-speaking APT group with low confidence and recommends monitoring ViPNet systems for traffic on ports 5003, 5060, and 443.
